root.label: Rights & Post-War Britain
root.gloss: Women’s suffrage, building the Welfare State and NHS, the Windrush pioneers, the 1963 Bristol Bus Boycott, and CND nuclear protest.

children.label: Part 1: Suffrage & Welfare State
children.gloss: Votes for women won in 1918 and Clement Attlee’s post-1945 creation of the Welfare State and free NHS.

children.label: 1. Votes for Women & 1918
children.gloss: Millicent Fawcett’s Suffragists, Emmeline Pankhurst’s WSPU Suffragettes, prison hunger strikes, and the 1918 franchise breakthrough.

children.label: Suffragists vs WSPU Militancy
children.gloss: Fawcett’s law-abiding NUWSS lobbied Parliament peacefully while Pankhurst’s 1903 WSPU embraced "Deeds, not words".

children.label: Fawcett’s 1897 Peaceful NUWSS
children.gloss: United 17 groups; 50,000+ members; Used petitions and parliamentary lobbying.

children.label: Pankhurst’s 1903 Militant WSPU
children.gloss: Adopted motto Deeds, not words; Chained to railings, disrupted rallies.

children.label: → Triggered Mass Holloway Arrests
children.gloss: Confronted police outside Buckingham Palace; Captured daily national newspaper headlines.

children.label: Peaceful Lobbying vs Direct Action
children.gloss: NUWSS proved mature democratic citizenship; WSPU forced issue onto agenda.

children.label: Hunger Strikes & Jiu-Jitsu Guard
children.gloss: Forced feeding, the 1913 Cat and Mouse Act, Edith Garrud’s jiu-jitsu Bodyguard, and Emily Davison’s Epsom Derby death.

children.label: Forced Feeding & 1913 Cat-Mouse
children.gloss: Rubber tubes shoved down throats; Released weak strikers, re-arrested later.

children.label: Garrud’s Bodyguard & Epsom 1913
children.gloss: 30 jiu-jitsu women hid clubs; Davison died under King’s horse.

children.label: → Public Outrage Over State Brutality
children.gloss: WSPU awarded silver hunger medals; Shamed Liberal government prison tactics.

children.label: Escalated Street Conflict Before WWI
children.gloss: Shielded Pankhurst from police batons; Created martyr at June Derby.

children.label: WWI Munitions & 1918 Vote
children.gloss: Wartime work by 1.5 million women broke parliamentary resistance, winning votes for 8.4 million women over 30 in 1918.

children.label: 1.5m Women Entered WWI Work
children.gloss: Suspended militant campaigning August 1914; Worked munitions, farms, and hospitals.

children.label: Feb 1918 Representation Act Passed
children.gloss: Enfranchised 8.4m women over thirty; Kept temporary property qualification rule.

children.label: → Ended Male Parliamentary Monopoly
children.gloss: Ended anti-suffrage parliamentary excuses; Opened path to equal franchise.

children.label: Combined Pre-War Campaign & War Service
children.gloss: Canary Girls proved patriotic duty; Crowned decades of suffrage campaigning.

children.label: 2. Welfare State & The NHS
children.gloss: Wartime evacuation, Beveridge’s Five Giants, Labour’s 1945 landslide, abolishing workhouses, and Aneurin Bevan’s free NHS.

children.label: Evacuation & Beveridge’s 5 Giants
children.gloss: Operation Pied Piper and Blitz solidarity inspired Sir William Beveridge’s bestselling 1942 blueprint to slay Five Giants.

children.label: 1.5m Evacuees & Blitz Solidarity
children.gloss: Exposed urban rickets and lice; Ration queues united social classes.

children.label: Dec 1942 Beveridge Report Sold 630k
children.gloss: Want, Disease, Ignorance, Squalor, Idleness; Promised cradle to grave security.

children.label: → Fuelled Demand for Fairer Britain
children.gloss: Queues formed outside government bookshops; Shaped Labour’s 1945 election pledge.

children.label: Blueprint for Modern Welfare State
children.gloss: Rejected pre-war destitution and charity; Redefined citizen social rights.

children.label: 1945 Attlee Win & Welfare Laws
children.gloss: Clement Attlee’s 146-seat Labour landslide enacted National Insurance (1946) and abolished Victorian Poor Law workhouses (1948).

children.label: July 1945 146-Seat Labour Landslide
children.gloss: Voters recalled 1930s Jarrow slump; Backed Let Us Face Future.

children.label: 1946 Insurance & 1948 Assistance Acts
children.gloss: Funded sickness, pensions, jobless pay; Abolished Victorian Poor Law workhouses.

children.label: → Built Universal State Safety Net
children.gloss: Weekly worker, employer, state payments; Protected citizens outside insurance too.

children.label: Ended Century of Workhouse Stigma
children.gloss: Replaced means-tested 1930s dole shame; Transformed post-war British citizenship.

children.label: Bevan, BMA & Free NHS (1948)
children.gloss: Health Minister Aneurin Bevan overcame BMA doctor resistance to launch universal free healthcare on 5 July 1948.

children.label: BMA Threatened Total Doctor Boycott
children.gloss: Resisted becoming salaried state workers; Endangered launch of national service.

children.label: Bevan’s Gold Deal & 5 July 1948
children.gloss: Allowed private beds inside hospitals; Opened NHS 5 July 1948.

children.label: → Free Healthcare at Delivery Point
children.gloss: Ended fear of doctor bills; Expanded hospital demand for staff.

children.label: Made Healthcare a Universal Right
children.gloss: Crowning pillar of Welfare State; Transformed health from private luxury.

children.label: Part 2: Windrush & Civil Rights
children.gloss: Caribbean pioneers aboard HMT Empire Windrush, Claudia Jones’s Carnival, the 1963 Bristol Bus Boycott, and Race Relations laws.

children.label: 3. Windrush & Notting Hill
children.gloss: Post-war labour recruitment and the 1948 Nationality Act brought Windrush pioneers who overcame colour bars and 1958 riots.

children.label: 1948 Nationality Act & Windrush
children.gloss: Recruited as CUKC British citizens to rebuild Britain, 492 Caribbean passengers docked at Tilbury on 22 June 1948.

children.label: NHS, Rail & Blitz Labour Shortage
children.gloss: Recruited workers across Commonwealth; 1948 Act gave 800m CUKC entry.

children.label: 22 June 1948 Windrush at Tilbury
children.gloss: 492 Caribbean pioneers came ashore; Lord Kitchener sang calypso onboard.

children.label: → Staffed Hospitals, Buses & Rail
children.gloss: Included RAF veterans and nurses; Held full British voting rights.

children.label: Foundation of Modern Multicultural UK
children.gloss: Arrived as legal British citizens; Rebuilt exhausted post-war infrastructure.

children.label: Colour Bar & Pardner Savings
children.gloss: Confronted by racist housing signs and bank refusals, Caribbean families pooled savings in cooperative "pardner" schemes.

children.label: Informal Housing & Bank Colour Bar
children.gloss: Window signs barred Black tenants; High-street banks refused home mortgages.

children.label: Cooperative Weekly Pardner Clubs
children.gloss: Pooled community savings each week; Rotated lump sums among families.

children.label: → Bought Freehold Urban Family Homes
children.gloss: Escaped damp overpriced boarding rooms; Built permanent inner-city communities.

children.label: Proved Grassroots Economic Resilience
children.gloss: Bypassed discriminatory British banking; Sustained family stability despite racism.

children.label: 1958 Riots & Claudia Jones
children.gloss: After violent 1958 Notting Hill Teddy Boy attacks, Claudia Jones founded the West Indian Gazette and 1959 Caribbean Carnival.

children.label: Aug 1958 Notting Hill Race Riots
children.gloss: White Teddy Boys used iron bars; Police offered Black residents little.

children.label: White Teddy Boys used iron bars
children.gloss: White Teddy Boys used iron bars

children.label: Claudia Jones & 1959 Carnival
children.gloss: Founded Brixton West Indian Gazette; Hosted St Pancras indoor carnival.

children.label: → Grew Into Notting Hill Carnival
children.gloss: Celebrated steel bands and dance; Gave community national political voice.

children.label: Turned Racist Trauma Into Pride
children.gloss: Asserted right to public joy; Reshaped modern British urban culture.

children.label: 4. Bristol Boycott & Race Laws
children.gloss: Paul Stephenson and the West Indian Development Council defeated Bristol’s bus colour bar, inspiring the 1965–68 Race Relations Acts.

children.label: Bus Colour Bar & Bailey Sting
children.gloss: Despite 200 vacancies, Bristol buses and local union officials barred Black crews until Paul Stephenson’s sting with Guy Bailey.

children.label: Company & TGWU Crew Colour Bar
children.gloss: Barred Black drivers despite 200 gaps; Local union backed white-only crews.

children.label: Stephenson’s Guy Bailey Test Case
children.gloss: Qualified 18-year-old Boys’ Brigade officer; Depot cancelled interview over race.

children.label: → Press Proof Ignited 30 Apr Boycott
children.gloss: Exposed undeniable racial ban publicly; Launched West Indian Development boycott.

children.label: Shattered Excuse of Unqualified Applicants
children.gloss: Caught state-owned firm red-handed; Put UK racism in headlines.

children.label: Four-Month Boycott Solidarity
children.gloss: Inspired by Montgomery, 3,000 West Indians, Bristol students, Tony Benn, and Harold Wilson forced the bus company’s surrender.

children.label: Citywide Walkout & Student Marches
children.gloss: Hackett, Henry, Evans led 3,000; Bristol University students picketed HQ.

children.label: Tony Benn & Wilson Backed Campaign
children.gloss: MP Benn boycotted racist union; Wilson pledged anti-racism law.

children.label: → Colour Bar Ended 28 August 1963
children.gloss: Same day as King’s Washington speech; Hired Sikh conductor Raghbir Singh.

children.label: Same day as King’s Washington speech
children.gloss: Same day as King’s Washington speech

children.label: Modelled Non-Violent UK Direct Action
children.gloss: Echoed 1955 Montgomery bus boycott; Slashed company ticket revenues fast.

children.label: 1965 & 1968 Race Relations Acts
children.gloss: Bristol’s victory propelled Harold Wilson’s government to pass Britain’s first statutory Race Relations Acts in 1965 and 1968.

children.label: Bristol Proved Need for National Law
children.gloss: No law barred colour bars 1963; Fulfilled Wilson’s 1963 rally pledge.

children.label: 1965 & 1968 Race Relations Acts
children.gloss: Banned discrimination in public places; 1968 outlawed housing, job bans.

children.label: → Ended Legal No-Blacks Signs
children.gloss: Created statutory civil rights framework; Protected minority workers and tenants.

children.label: Watershed in British Equality Law
children.gloss: Citizen protest reshaped national statute; Laid groundwork for equality laws.

children.label: Part 3: Nuclear Fear & Protest
children.gloss: Britain’s A-bomb and H-bomb tests, CND and Aldermaston marches, secret ROC bunkers, Protect and Survive, and Greenham Common.

children.label: 5. H-Bomb, CND & Greenham
children.gloss: From Britain’s 1952–57 nuclear tests and Gerald Holtom’s CND peace symbol to York’s bunker and Greenham Common.

children.label: UK Bombs, CND & Peace Symbol
children.gloss: Britain’s 1952 atomic and 1957 H-bomb tests sparked the 1958 founding of CND and Gerald Holtom’s semaphore peace symbol.

children.label: 1952 Hurricane & 1957 H-Bomb Tests
children.gloss: Third nuclear power Australia 1952; Tested Malden Island H-bomb 1957.

children.label: Feb 1958 CND & Holtom’s Logo
children.gloss: Russell and Collins sought unilateralism; Combined naval semaphore N and D.

children.label: Combined naval semaphore N and D
children.gloss: Combined naval semaphore N and D

children.label: → Launched Easter 1958 Aldermaston March
children.gloss: Rallied horror at radioactive fallout; Created universal global peace symbol.

children.label: Challenged UK Nuclear Deterrent Policy
children.gloss: Attlee and Churchill backed deterrent; CND urged moral unilateral scrapping.

children.label: Aldermaston & Secret York Bunker
children.gloss: Tens of thousands marched 52 miles to Aldermaston while the Home Office built 29 secret ROC bunkers with zero public shelters.

children.label: 52-Mile Easter 1958 Peace March
children.gloss: Walked four days to Berkshire; Students, families, and jazz bands.

children.label: 1961 Secret York ROC Bunker
children.gloss: Built 29 regional underground centres; 60 volunteers sealed 30 days.

children.label: → Exposed Elite vs Civilian Shelter Gap
children.gloss: Plotted fallout plumes underground; Gave ordinary families zero bunkers.

children.label: Birthed Post-War Youth Counter-Culture
children.gloss: Brought generational protest to streets; Questioned state Cold War secrecy.

children.label: Protect & Survive to Greenham
children.gloss: Mockery of the 1980 Protect and Survive booklet fuelled E. P. Thompson’s critique and the 30,000-woman Greenham Common protest.

children.label: 1980 Protect & Survive Booklet
children.gloss: Four-minute nuclear warning sirens; Advised wooden door mattress shelters.

children.label: 1982 Greenham Common Embrace Base
children.gloss: Thompson wrote Protest and Survive; 30,000 women encircled 9-mile fence.

children.label: → Revived Mass 1980s Anti-Nuclear Wave
children.gloss: Protested US cruise missile base; Exposed futility of DIY shelters.

children.label: Landmark Feminist Peace Direct Action
children.gloss: Maintained women’s camp at gates; Turned civil defence into satire.
